stories.title: Govt increases wheat import ceiling to curb price increases
summary: ISLAMABAD: The government on Friday decided to increase the wheat import ceiling by 150 per cent to 2.5 million tonnes to check continuously rising prices of wheat and wheat flour in the market.

The decision was taken after detailed consideration of a summary submitted by the Ministry of National Food Security and Research, seeking the enhancement of the previously approved wheat import ceiling from one million tonnes to 2.5 MMT.

The ECC agreed that enhancing the import ceiling to 2.5 MMT would provide enough flexibility to meet additional provincial requirements or shortfalls in available stocks, without requiring repeated approvals.

stories.title: Makkah pact nations review regional security, condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
summary: A meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement’s top decision-making body on Friday reviewed the regional security situation and condemned “persistent and heinous” Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
The SPDC, which brings together the foreign and defence ministers and chiefs of defence staff of the three countries, is the alliance’s principal decision-making forum.

Managing relations with Iran will be particularly important for Pakistan, which has sought to preserve diplomatic engagement with Tehran while deepening defence cooperation with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

stories.title: President Zardari, PML-Q chief Shujaat discuss country's political situation
summary: President Asif Ali Zardari on Friday discussed the country’s political situation in a meeting with former prime minister and Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) chief Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain.
Earlier this week, Naqvi also held a meeting with Shujaat, where the debate over the creation of new provinces and devolution of powers was discussed.
In the meeting, Naqvi and Shujaat discussed the overall political situation, measures to maintain law and order, and the need to transfer power to the grassroots level.

stories.title: 3 convicted of taking woman from UK to Pakistan, forcing her into marriage: police
summary: Police in the United Kingdom said on Friday that three people had been convicted of taking a young woman from the country to Pakistan and forcing her into marriage.

Officers detained the three on Nov 7, 2024 at Birmingham Airport on suspicion of forced marriage. “We also safeguarded the woman and, after speaking to her, we established she was unaware how she had been exploited,” the police said.
Following the trial at Birmingham Crown Court, Bashir, aged 55, Bi, 55, and Aktar, 38, were convicted of the offence and will be sentenced at a later date, the statement said.

stories.title: Man buried under rubble rescued alive 2 days after building collapse in Karachi’s Baloch Colony
summary: KARACHI: A man buried under the rubble from the collapse of an under-construction six-storey building near Karachi’s Baloch Colony was rescued alive on Friday, two days after the incident occurred.
According to the statement, the chief minister directed rescue agencies and the Karachi commissioner to accelerate the ongoing rescue operation and deploy all available resources.
The building’s four owners — including Salman Tahir whose arrest the Sindh CM has ordered — its builder, architect, structural engineer and its contractors have been nominated in the FIR.

stories.title: SBP issues Rs200 commemorative coin to mark Mata Sahib Hasi Devi’s 200th birth anniversary
summary: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) has issued a Rs200 commemorative coin to mark the 200th birth anniversary of Pujya Mata Sahib Hasi Devi, the bank said in a statement on Friday.
The inscription “Pujya Mata Sahib Hasi Devi” appears at the top along the periphery, while the wording “200th birth anniversary” is written along the lower periphery.

Last month, Pakistan Post also issued two special commemorative postage stamps and a souvenir sheet for the 200th birth anniversary of Mata Sahib Hasi Devi to promote interfaith harmony and Sufi traditions in the region.

stories.title: Indian police say they rescued 164 foreigners trafficked for cyber fraud
summary: Indian police said they had rescued 164 foreign nationals allegedly trafficked into the country and forced to commit online fraud, in a rare case involving victims from overseas.
Fraud compounds, where international scammers lure internet users into fake romantic relationships, cryptocurrency investments and betting platforms, are common in Southeast Asia.
A United Nations report estimated this year that at least 300,000 people have been trafficked into scam compounds across Southeast Asia.

stories.title: Roads blocked, traffic congested in Karachi for 2nd consecutive day
summary: Traffic travelling from Sharea Faisal towards the airport would be diverted right from Avari traffic signal onto Fatima Jinnah Road, towards Cantt, School Road, CSD and Kala Pul, the release said.
According to updates issued by the traffic police, the road from Coast Guard towards Zainab Market and Sarwar Shaheed Road was closed to traffic at around 3:20pm in view of security.
Traffic is being sent via Avari Towers towards Fatima Jinnah Road, police said.

stories.title: Short-term inflation clocks in at 9.49pc driven by wheat flour prices
summary: ISLAMABAD: Short-term inflation was recorded at 9.49 per cent year-on-year in the week ending on Nov 26, driven largely by wheat flour prices, according to official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) on Friday.

Items that recorded week-on-week price declines included tomatoes (23.92pc), onions (21.27pc), LPG (7.78pc), petrol (2.48pc), diesel (1.99pc), pulse masoor (0.68pc), sugar (0.24pc) and bananas & pulse mash (0.12pc) each.
Last week, short-term inflation was recorded at 10.41pc year-on-year, driven largely by wheat flour prices.

stories.title: Airline Norse Atlantic's Norwegian operating unit declares bankruptcy
summary: Airline Norse Atlantic’s Norwegian operating unit has declared bankruptcy, the long-haul budget carrier said on Friday, succumbing to soaring fuel costs wrought by the war on Iran.
Norse in 2021 signed long-term leases for nine Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft from Ireland-based AerCap Holdings and six Dreamliners from Singapore-based BOC Aviation Ltd.

In October, PIA signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Nov 1.

stories.title: ADB approves $468m in loans to boost water, agriculture management in KP and Punjab
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Friday approved two loans totalling $468 million to improve water and agriculture management in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Punjab.

Valued at Rs69.893bn, the KP Resilient Irrigated Agriculture Livelihoods Development Project aims to rehabilitate the Pehur Main Canal, construct the Mulkhow Irrigation Distribution System and extend the Pehur High Level Canal.

The project aims to introduce modern spate irrigation systems, flood-protection channels, telemetry systems and centralised supervisory control and data acquisition monitoring to strengthen regional water security.

stories.title: Government reduces petrol price by Re1, keeps diesel unchanged
summary: According to a notification issued by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra), petrol will be sold at Rs312 per litre, while HSD will remain priced at Rs346 per litre.
The latest revision comes a day after the government cut petrol prices by Re1 per litre and HSD by Rs2 per litre for November 27.

Read: Govt cuts petrol by Re1, diesel by Rs2 for Nov 27 On November 2, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: PM calls for effective guidance, simplified procedures for SMEs seeking financial support
summary: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday called for better guidance for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) seeking financing from banks, enabling access to loans through simplified procedures.

Presiding over a meeting on facilitating access to credit for SMEs, the premier termed these enterprises the “backbone” of the country’s economy. “Facilitating them will boost economic activity, employment and business opportunities,” the prime minister said.

The prime minister directed the provision of effective guidance and support to SMEs to improve their access to financial resources, prepare business documentation and benefit from opportunities in the export sector.

stories.title: No threat to government as PM Shehbaz-CDF Munir partnership continues: Talal Chaudhry
summary: Speaking on a private television programme, Naya Pakistan, Chaudhry said the government believed in political consultations and that all major decisions were taken after bringing coalition partners on board.
Referring to Fazl's recent remarks, Chaudhry said the political resentment and anger in the JUI-F chief's statements were evident in his interviews and public appearances.
And if a government was formed in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, why was he not made its head?” Chaudhry said, describing what he believed to be the reasons behind Fazl's anger.

stories.title: Pakistan seeks deeper cooperation with IAEA on nuclear security
summary: The statement came as the 15th annual meeting of the International Network for Nuclear Security Training and Support Centres (NSSC Network), hosted by Pakistan in collaboration with the IAEA, concluded in Islamabad.
The IAEA’s unit head of the Division of Nuclear Security commended Pakistan for hosting the meeting, describing it as an important milestone in international nuclear security cooperation.
Its return to Pakistan after a decade reflected the country’s sustained engagement with the IAEA and continued contribution to international nuclear security cooperation, the statement added.

stories.title: After water and sports, India takes aim at Pakistani entertainment
summary: India's campaign to isolate Pakistan appears to be extending beyond water and sport into art and culture, with an Indian film industry organisation demanding a permanent ban on Pakistani entertainment content, including Netflix’s upcoming first Pakistani original series.

In a letter dated November 24, the association called for strict legal action and penalties against over-the-top (OTT) platforms streaming Pakistani films, dramas, songs, podcasts and other entertainment content in India.
Some have argued that if Pakistani entertainment is unwelcome in India, the streaming platform should also reconsider the availability of Indian content in Pakistan.

stories.title: FO says reports of boat carrying Pakistani migrants capsizing off Libya remain unverified
summary: It was reported earlier this week that at least 25 people from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bajaur district were feared dead or missing after a migrant boat capsized near Libya.

Previous boat tragedies In April this year, more than 80 migrants including 20 Pakistanis were reported missing after a boat carrying around 120 people capsized in the Central Mediterranean after departing from Libya.
In October last year, 18 migrants were killed when a wooden vessel capsized off the coast of Libya, while 64 people, including 12 Pakistanis, were reported missing.

stories.title: Quetta Gladiators dismiss sale rumours, reaffirm commitment to PSL
summary: Quetta Gladiators have dismissed speculation about a possible sale of the franchise or an exit from the Pakistan Super League (PSL), reaffirming their financial stability and commitment to the competition.

He also welcomed the recent direct signings of international players by PSL franchises, including New Zealand fast bowler Lockie Ferguson by Quetta Gladiators, describing the developments as evidence of the league’s growing strength.

The franchise thanked the Pakistan Cricket Board, PSL management, commercial partners and supporters for their continued backing, expressing confidence that Quetta Gladiators would remain in safe hands.

stories.title: Fleeing murder suspect crashes into elephant in Sri Lanka
summary: A Sri Lankan man suspected of fatally stabbing a woman was arrested on Friday after he crashed his scooter into a wild elephant as he attempted to escape, police said.
The 49-year-old man is accused of stabbing the woman in her home in the northern district of Anuradhapura, a police official told AFP.
However, his attempted escape ended when his scooter crashed into the elephant as it emerged from the jungle onto the road a short distance away, the official said.

stories.title: FIR over Karachi building collapse omits government officials despite SBCA action
summary: A six-storey under-construction building in Karachi collapsed on Wednesday, killing eight people and injuring 14 others.

The absence of any government official among the nominated accused raises questions about the scope of the investigation, particularly the role of regulatory authorities responsible for overseeing construction and enforcing building regulations.

Read: Karachi building collapse: Death toll rises to eight as rescue efforts continue Meanwhile, the death toll from the tragedy rose to eight today, while more than 10 people are still feared trapped beneath the rubble.

stories.title: Indian police say they dismantled international cyber fraud ring, rescued 164 foreigners
summary: Police in India have said they rescued ​dozens of Malaysian and Indonesian ‌nationals who were illegally confined and forced to participate in a cyber fraud ​operation in a suburb of national ​capital Delhi.

They were lured to India with promises of employment ​and "lucrative opportunities", but were later ​forced to participate in the scam that ‌cheated ⁠unsuspecting people through fake investment schemes, police said.
Police said the foreign nationals had been brought to India under various pretexts, including promises of jobs and lucrative opportunities.

stories.title: ECP says it cannot force parties to field women on winnable seats
summary: The ECP said it had informed the Sub-Committee of the National Assembly’s Special Committee on Gender Mainstreaming at the time that, under the existing electoral laws, the authority to award tickets to women rested with the political party concerned.
Section 206 of the Elections Act, 2017, requires every political party to award at least five per cent of its tickets on general seats to women candidates.
The NA body has now urged the ECP to ensure that the quota translates into meaningful representation by requiring political parties to field women candidates in winnable constituencies.

stories.title: Bilawal says South Punjab has constitutional right to separate province, opposes dividing Punjab into four
summary: Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Friday voiced support for the creation of a separate South Punjab province, saying it was the "wish of the people", but opposed dividing Punjab into four provinces.

Addressing a public rally in Rahim Yar Khan, Bilawal said he supported the creation of South Punjab in line with the people's wishes, stressing that the PPP had never "abandoned" its workers and would continue to stand by them.
He stated: "I support the creation of a South Punjab province because it is the people's wish.

stories.title: Islamabad police announce road closures, traffic diversions ahead of foreign delegations' arrival
summary: Ahead of the arrival of foreign delegations in the federal capital on Friday, Islamabad police issued traffic advisories outlining road closures and alternative routes for commuters.

Police said on Friday that entry and exit routes to and from the Red Zone, including those around Serena Hotel, Nadra Chowk, Ayub Chowk and Express Chowk, would remain closed from Thursday until 12:30am on Saturday.
Drivers heading to the New Islamabad International Airport and Peshawar Road were advised to use Jinnah Avenue and Margalla Road, police said.

stories.title: Major storm batters US on Thanksgiving holiday
summary: A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Friday, as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history.
Stay safe While flooding was reported up and down the East Coast, impacts were also felt inland, with powerful gusts and inundated soil leading to trees tumbling over onto power lines and homes.
Officials urged people to limit road travel, while several major bridges were closed due to high winds.

stories.title: What is Modi's automated takedown law, which has embroiled Meta in a political storm?
summary: Meta's online disclosures show it restricted access to 5.44 million items of content in India in the first half of 2026, about 130 times ​the 41,357 restricted in the previous six months.

Meta's 5.44 million ​content restrictions in India were second only ⁠to Indonesia, where the number stood at 20.6 million, but the company says over 20 million of those were "for alleged violation of local laws on gambling".

The Indian Youth Congress' lawsuit, filed by lawyer Rishav Ranjan, argues that Meta has made some posts of the political group's members "unavailable in India" and that the automated system is catching far more than "exactly identical" copies.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz directs steps to simplify loan procedures for SMEs
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday directed the relevant authorities to simplify loan procedures for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and ease their access to finance to boost economic activity, create jobs, and promote entrepreneurship.

Chairing a high-level meeting in Islamabad on improving access to credit for SMEs, PM Shehbaz stressed the need to provide SMEs with effective guidance and support in accessing financial resources, preparing business documentation and capitalising on export opportunities.

Emphasising the need for comprehensive banking support, the premier said banks should assist SMEs not only through loans but also by facilitating the issuance of Letters of Credit (LCs) and bank guarantees.

stories.title: India-US trade agreement nearing completion: Indian commerce minister
summary: Goyal’s comments came after US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on Wednesday said Indian goods would face tariffs of 17 per cent if a trade deal is reached but rise to as much as 25pc if not.

Last month, New Delhi’s Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said trade deal talks between India and US had reached a “plateau”, after negotiations dragged on for months with the sides struggling to resolve sticking points.
On Wednesday, the US unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies, including India, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production.

stories.title: PSX sheds 397 points amid profit-taking
summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) closed the week on a subdued note on Friday, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index shedding nearly 400 points as geopolitical uncertainty and rollover-related profit-taking weighed on investor sentiment.
The market opened on a weak note amid persistent geopolitical tensions and continued profit-taking on the final trading day of the rollover week ahead of the weekend.

The benchmark remained range-bound throughout the session and closed near its intraday low, as intermittent value buying failed to trigger a meaningful recovery, reflecting cautious investor sentiment, said Deputy Head of Trading at Arif Habib Ltd Ali Najib.

stories.title: Lahore police chief denies Fazl’s arrest
summary: Fazl’s late-night claim of his arrest came as authorities barred him and eight other leaders of his party from entering, residing or remaining in Sargodha — where the JUI-F planned to hold a rally on Thursday — for 30 days.
In the video posted on the JUI-F’s X account, Fazl asked his party workers and supporters to postpone protests and sit-ins.
Fazl-govt rift On Tuesday, JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman claimed he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to restrict his movement.

stories.title: Shahid Khaqan Abbasi warns against referendum on new provinces without a clear roadmap
summary: Do not play foul with the people!” The former premier opined that the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) government appeared reluctant to create new provinces because the process could lead to fresh elections.

The debate around provinces gained momentum on July 31, when Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi called for the creation of additional provinces or administrative units, arguing that Pakistan's existing governance structure was outdated and required a comprehensive overhaul.
Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has supported the idea of creating at least 12 provinces, arguing that smaller administrative units could improve governance and service delivery.

stories.title: New York bans AI chatbot toys for 5 years over child safety concerns
summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has signed legislation imposing a five-year ban on the manufacture, distribution, and sale of children's toys equipped with artificial intelligence companion chatbots, citing concerns over child safety and privacy.
The law, signed Tuesday, targets toys such as talking stuffed animals, dolls, and robots that use internet-connected AI chatbots to hold conversations with children.

"Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk," Hochul said in a statement.

stories.title: ASI demoted, Golra SHO’s pay cut over flawed theft probe
summary: ISLAMABAD: An investigation officer (IO) was demoted and a station house officer (SHO) faced a two-stage reduction in pay for poor investigation and supervision of a theft case, a police official said on Wednesday.
The IO, an assistant sub-inspector (ASI), was demoted to the rank of head constable, while the pay of the SHO of Golra Police Station was reduced by two stages.

DIG Islamabad Ali Wasim emphasised that all officers must perform their duties with dedication and ensure effective coordination to control crime and maintain law and order. “Protection of citizens’ lives and property is the foremost priority of Islamabad Police,” he said.

stories.title: Overton takes 5-12 as England thrash Australia in third T20
summary: Jamie Overton took a career-best 5-12 as England thrashed Australia by seven wickets in the third T20 international in Brisbane on Friday.
"I thought Jamie Overton was outstanding tonight," England captain Harry Brook said.
Harper raced to 26 off 14 balls before Dawson grabbed his second when the Australian wicketkeeper got a top edge to Overton at mid-on.

stories.title: Trump backs Iraqi leader's efforts to assert more state authority
summary: United States President Donald Trump on Friday backed the Iraqi leader's drive to assert state control, including stopping the smuggling of Iraqi oil, moves that put Baghdad in direct confrontation with Iran's militia allies and Kurdish authorities.
Speaking to the Iraqi state news agency, Aboudi added that Iraq lost an estimated $100 billion to oil smuggling through its Kurdistan region from 2008 to 2025.

Iraq on Thursday closed two border crossings in the Kurdistan region, one with Syria and one with Iran, after Zaidi ordered federal authorities to take control of crossings run by the semi-autonomous regional government.

stories.title: LHC seeks replies on plea by five Afghan medical students over MBBS registration
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Friday issued notices to the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) and other respondents on a petition filed by five Afghan medical students seeking registration to sit their first professional MBBS examination in January.
In September, the LHC suspended the operation of PMDC directives ordering Afghan medical students to return to Afghanistan.

The PMDC barred medical and dental colleges from admitting or placing Afghan students for the current academic session and said those already enrolled in such programmes were required to return to Afghanistan.

stories.title: 'Construction continued in broad daylight': Residents see greed, official negligence behind Baloch Colony building collapse
summary: 'Construction continued in broad daylight': Residents see greed, official negligence behind Baloch Colony building collapse

stories.title: From skipping class to 50th NZ Test cap for emotional Blundell
summary: When Tom Blundell made his Test debut for New Zealand against the West Indies in December 2017, he walked back to his Wellington home from the Basin Reserve still wearing his match whites.
On Friday, Blundell won his 50th Test cap for New Zealand while hitting a fighting, unbeaten 53 to put his country in prime position at the end of the first day against India in Christchurch.

"But being able to represent New Zealand 50 times in Test cricket is pretty special to me and I love this team and the people in it." The number Blundell doesn't care much for are his impressive batting figures compiled over the past nine years.

stories.title: Binance says 'withdrawal recovery work' complete after $6.3 billion crypto heist
summary: "Our withdrawal recovery work is completed, and the withdrawal suspension from the ​security incident has been fully lifted," ​it said in an X post on Thursday.

Separately, a small number are temporarily paused due to network maintenance, which… pic.twitter.com/QZmXhsc2qA — Binance (@binance) November 26, 2026 "Withdrawals are ‌open ⁠across nearly all networks.
